title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #2

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The kayamba is a shaker used mainly at the (1 mark)
   A. North of Lake Victoria only
   B. Kenyan highlands only
   C. Kenyan coast
   D. Northern desert only

2. Isukuti is a lively drum dance of the (1 mark)
   A. Turkana
   B. Luhya
   C. Maasai
   D. Somali

3. Claves are (1 mark)
   A. drums with strings
   B. a kind of flute
   C. a horn
   D. two wooden sticks hit together

4. What can be used as the core of an improvised macramé ball? (1 mark)
   A. A large stone
   B. Crumpled paper or old cloth
   C. A metal nail
   D. A glass bottle

5. Which is a good safety rule before playing netball? (1 mark)
   A. Play on broken ground
   B. Remove rings and bracelets
   C. Wear a necklace
   D. Play with long sharp nails

6. How is flour paste made? (1 mark)
   A. Mix flour and cold water to a smooth paste, then add hot water while stirring
   B. Mix flour and sand
   C. Freeze flour
   D. Burn flour

7. To paint an object so it looks round, you should (1 mark)
   A. paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   B. leave it blank
   C. use one flat colour only
   D. paint it black

8. How many boxes are on the scale strip in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. One
   B. Five
   C. Two
   D. Ten

9. Overlapping in a montage means (1 mark)
   A. pieces are painted black
   B. one piece partly covers another
   C. pieces are cut into tiny bits
   D. pieces are far apart

10. Why should your composed rhythm be your own idea? (1 mark)
   A. To use more paper
   B. Original work shows honesty
   C. To finish faster
   D. To be different from the teacher only

11. A rhythmic pattern feels finished when it ends on (1 mark)
   A. a mistake
   B. a long note
   C. a rest
   D. a very short note

12. Which of these letters has a tail below the baseline? (1 mark)
   A. l
   B. y
   C. h
   D. d

13. The Kodaly hand sign for d is (1 mark)
   A. a sloping palm
   B. a flat hand held level
   C. a closed fist
   D. a pointing finger

14. Which tune ends on the home note? (1 mark)
   A. d r m r
   B. m r m r
   C. d r m r d
   D. r m r m

15. Pitch means (1 mark)
   A. how high or low a sound is
   B. how loud a sound is
   C. how long a sound lasts
   D. the speed of a song

16. Stepwise motion means the tune moves (1 mark)
   A. to the next note above or below
   B. down only
   C. by big jumps
   D. only on one note

17. Which is part of a good warm-up? (1 mark)
   A. Eating a large meal
   B. Gentle jogging and stretching
   C. Sitting still
   D. Sleeping

18. Compared with the medium start, the elongated start has the back knee (1 mark)
   A. on the line
   B. further back
   C. further forward
   D. in the air

19. Why do we warm up before sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. To make the track smooth
   B. To prepare muscles and avoid injury
   C. To hide from the starter
   D. To tire out the muscles

20. What should you do if something hurts during gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Push a friend
   B. Hide it
   C. Keep going
   D. Stop and tell your teacher

21. Good manners for an audience include (1 mark)
   A. walking around
   B. talking loudly
   C. being quiet and clapping at the right time
   D. throwing things

22. In a folk song, the singer who leads is called the (1 mark)
   A. listener
   B. drummer
   C. umpire
   D. soloist

23. How should you behave when the anthem is sung? (1 mark)
   A. Stand straight and quietly
   B. Play games
   C. Talk to friends
   D. Run around

24. The mood of a song is (1 mark)
   A. its length in metres
   B. the name of the composer
   C. its price
   D. the feeling it gives

25. A topical song is (1 mark)
   A. about the moon only
   B. always sad
   C. about a topic that matters at a certain time
   D. without a tune

26. Which is a patriotic song? (1 mark)
   A. A lullaby about sleeping
   B. A drum solo
   C. Kenya National Anthem
   D. A hymn of worship only

27. Singing softly at the end of a lullaby shows (1 mark)
   A. a high pitch only
   B. a soft dynamic
   C. a fast tempo
   D. a loud dynamic

28. A blurred photograph is (1 mark)
   A. not sharp
   B. very clear
   C. dark
   D. always good

29. For a well-lit photograph of a person, the sun should be (1 mark)
   A. behind the photographer
   B. under the ground
   C. inside the lens
   D. behind the person

30. Another name for the descant recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. soprano recorder
   B. bass recorder
   C. drum
   D. xylophone

31. The descant recorder is played by (1 mark)
   A. blowing air into it
   B. plucking strings
   C. striking it
   D. shaking it

32. Why should you not dive into shallow water? (1 mark)
   A. You can hit the bottom and hurt your head or neck
   B. It makes splashes
   C. It looks silly
   D. It makes noise

33. In a prone float, you keep your body (1 mark)
   A. stiff and bent
   B. curled with head up
   C. standing
   D. long and relaxed with face in the water

34. Why do we shower before entering the pool? (1 mark)
   A. To keep the pool clean
   B. To learn to float
   C. To get dry
   D. To warm the water

35. In the hawk and the chicks game, the hen (1 mark)
   A. chases the hawk away for ever
   B. sits down
   C. tags everyone
   D. protects the chicks

36. Which Kiswahili word means crab? (1 mark)
   A. mamba
   B. simba
   C. chura
   D. kaa

37. Which Kiswahili word means snake? (1 mark)
   A. tumbili
   B. chura
   C. kuku
   D. nyoka

38. The hare hop is done (1 mark)
   A. by sitting
   B. by rolling
   C. by crawling
   D. by hopping forward with both feet like a hare

39. How can you decorate a portfolio cover? (1 mark)
   A. By putting sand on it
   B. By burning it
   C. By pasting coloured paper or fabric
   D. By tearing it

40. The Kenya National Anthem is called (1 mark)
   A. Malaika
   B. Jambo Bwana
   C. Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   D. Twinkle Twinkle Little Star

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe the steps of a glide. (4 marks)

42. Write rhythm patterns for the elephant walk and the hare hop using rhythm names. (3 marks)

43. Name two types of songs learnt in this topic other than folk songs. (2 marks)

44. State four things to think about when analysing an art work. (4 marks)

45. Describe how to do the crab walk and name the muscles it strengthens. (3 marks)

46. How should you behave when the Kenya National Anthem is sung? (3 marks)

47. Describe a full netball court. (3 marks)

48. Give four ways in which gymnastics helps the body. (4 marks)

49. Why should the flag stick be held high while cheering? (2 marks)

50. Describe how to do the side roll safely. (4 marks)

51. How can you show the mood of a joyful song when singing? (3 marks)

52. Describe the steps for painting a picture of one object that shows colour value. (5 marks)

53. State two ways of playing percussion instruments. (2 marks)

54. Why is gymnastics not a race? (2 marks)

55. Why is it important to appreciate the percussion instruments of different communities? (3 marks)

56. Explain how to make a shade of green. (2 marks)

57. Explain how good singing performance is achieved, using posture, breathing, diction, expression and etiquette. (5 marks)

58. Why is it important not to share a recorder before cleaning it? (3 marks)

59. State the role of the Kenya National Anthem. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Kenyan coast
   The kayamba is a coastal shaker used by the Mijikenda and other coastal people.

2. B — Luhya
   Isukuti is played by the Luhya people, especially the Isukha and Idakho.

3. D — two wooden sticks hit together
   Claves are two hardwood sticks that are struck together.

4. B — Crumpled paper or old cloth
   Paper or cloth makes a soft core that keeps its shape.

5. B — Remove rings and bracelets
   Jewellery can hurt you and others.

6. A — Mix flour and cold water to a smooth paste, then add hot water while stirring
   An adult adds hot water to thicken the smooth paste.

7. A — paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   Tones make an object look solid and round.

8. B — Five
   The strip is divided into five equal boxes.

9. B — one piece partly covers another
   Overlapping helps to fill gaps and make the montage full.

10. B — Original work shows honesty
   Creating your own pattern shows integrity.

11. B — a long note
   Ending on a crotchet, a long note, makes it sound complete.

12. B — y
   The letter y has a tail below the baseline.

13. C — a closed fist
   Doh is shown with a fist.

14. C — d r m r d
   Only d r m r d ends on d.

15. A — how high or low a sound is
   Pitch is the highness or lowness of a note.

16. A — to the next note above or below
   Steps go to a neighbouring note.

17. B — Gentle jogging and stretching
   Jogging and stretching prepare the body.

18. B — further back
   Elongated means longer, so the feet are further apart.

19. B — To prepare muscles and avoid injury
   Warm muscles work better and are less likely to be hurt.

20. D — Stop and tell your teacher
   Pain is a warning, so stop and tell the teacher.

21. C — being quiet and clapping at the right time
   The audience should listen respectfully.

22. D — soloist
   The soloist sings the lead part.

23. A — Stand straight and quietly
   An anthem is sung with respect.

24. D — the feeling it gives
   Mood is the feeling of a song, such as joy or calm.

25. C — about a topic that matters at a certain time
   Topical songs give messages about topics such as health, safety or the environment.

26. C — Kenya National Anthem
   The anthem is a patriotic song.

27. B — a soft dynamic
   Softness is dynamics.

28. A — not sharp
   Blurred means not sharp.

29. A — behind the photographer
   Light falls on the front of the subject.

30. A — soprano recorder
   The descant is the soprano recorder.

31. A — blowing air into it
   A recorder is a wind instrument that you blow.

32. A — You can hit the bottom and hurt your head or neck
   Shallow water is dangerous for diving.

33. D — long and relaxed with face in the water
   A long relaxed body floats better.

34. A — To keep the pool clean
   It removes dirt and sweat.

35. D — protects the chicks
   The hen blocks the hawk.

36. D — kaa
   Kaa is a crab.

37. D — nyoka
   Nyoka is a snake.

38. D — by hopping forward with both feet like a hare
   Small quick hops.

39. C — By pasting coloured paper or fabric
   Decorating uses local resources.

40. C — Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   The Kiswahili title is Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stand with the back to the wall and arms stretched overhead. Put the feet on the wall and bend the knees. Take a breath and put the face in. Push off gently with the body straight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Elephant walk: taa taa taa (rest). Hare hop: ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pattern, 1 mark for correct rest or names.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sacred songs, patriotic songs and topical songs. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Aesthetic, skills, message and behaviour. Feedback is also accepted.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit, put hands behind, lift the hips and walk on hands and feet with tummy up. It strengthens the arms, shoulders and tummy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 1 mark for walking, 1 mark for muscles.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stand straight and still, face the flag, remove your cap, sing clearly and do not talk or play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is a rectangle 30.5 metres long and 15.25 metres wide. It is divided into three equal thirds. It has a goal post at each end with a goal circle and a centre circle in the middle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rectangle with measurements, 1 mark for thirds, 1 mark for circles or posts.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Makes muscles stronger; improves flexibility; improves balance and coordination; exercises the heart and lungs; builds confidence. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: So it does not hit other people, and so the flag can be seen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Lie on the back with body straight. Stretch the arms overhead with palms together and legs together. Tighten the tummy and point the toes. Roll over on to the side and tummy in a straight line. Get up slowly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Smile, use lively gestures, sing brightly and at a lively tempo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose an object and place it near a window. Draw the outline lightly. Mix the main colour and paint the object. Add a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side. Blend the edges and add a shadow, then let it dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five clear steps.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Striking and shaking. Scraping is also correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is about control and quality of movement, not about speed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for control, 1 mark for not speed.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: They show the culture and skill of each community. They help us respect one another. They should be preserved for future generations.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Add a small amount of black to green, and more if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for black, 1 mark for adding a little.

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: Stand tall with a relaxed body. Breathe deeply and sing on the breath. Say the words clearly. Use gestures and facial expressions to show the message and mood. Walk on and off quietly and respect others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five points.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Germs from the mouth can spread illnesses such as colds through the mouthpiece.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for the mouth or mouthpiece, 1 mark for spreading illness.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is a national symbol that unites Kenyans, shows love for the country and reminds us of our values.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
